name: Feminism
summary: Feminism is a family of movements and theories that seek equality of the sexes in political, economic, personal and social life. It holds that societies have been organized in ways that favor men, and works to end that through legal reform, challenges to gender roles and stereotypes, reproductive rights and protection from violence. Liberal, socialist, radical and intersectional strands differ on how deep the change must go and on issues such as sex work.
scope: The mainstream of contemporary feminism, drawing on the liberal, socialist/materialist, radical and intersectional strands as described in the SEP and Wikipedia, with the founding demands of Seneca Falls (1848) as its primary text. Where strands differ, answers are marked 0 or low confidence; trans-exclusionary radical feminism and anti-feminist currents are not followed.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Feminist political thought stresses public provision for reproductive health and the unequal distribution of care, so adherents generally back universal healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the aim of equal pay and economic justice for women, who are over-represented in low-wage work.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred from the widespread feminist critique of neoliberalism and of capitalism's reliance on unpaid care labor.

public-ownership.rationale: Socialist feminists would agree while liberal feminists would not, so adherents are split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the redistributive and care-supporting commitments of most feminist currents.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the focus on workers' rights and economic exclusion, which socialist and liberal feminists share.

property-fundamental.rationale: Feminists fought for women's property rights, but socialist and radical strands reject treating property as near-inviolable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from the common feminist critique of neoliberalism and demand for workplace protections.

cut-welfare.rationale: Feminists stress dependency and care needs and support social provision rather than cutting it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist feminists favor it while liberal feminists do not.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Feminism has no settled position; protection from violence and civil-liberties worries pull in different directions.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not a feminist question as such; adherents hold varied views.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Radical feminists such as MacKinnon favor regulating subordinating speech while liberal feminists resist, so adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on equal participation and deliberation and suspicion of concentrated power.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberal feminists treat the state as a tool for protecting rights and radicals want structures overhauled, not abolished, so the state is not seen as unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from feminist campaigns against domestic violence, which often include firearm restrictions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from distrust of coercive institutions, though adherents want better protection from violence.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Feminists are divided between those who treat sex work as labor and those who see it as exploitation.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the generally reformist and equality-oriented outlook of feminist criminology.

traditional-family.rationale: Feminists challenge traditional gender roles and treat the family as a source of women's subordination, while supporting equal rights within marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Contemporary mainstream and intersectional feminism supports LGBT equality, though some radical strands criticize marriage as an institution.

abortion-legal.rationale: Access to contraception and legal abortion is a defining feminist demand.

more-religion-public.rationale: Feminists historically objected to women's subordinate role in churches, though feminist theology exists in many faiths.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Intersectional feminism, following Crenshaw and hooks, links feminism to opposing racial domination.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sex/gender distinction and Beauvoir's idea that one becomes a woman make gender's social shaping central to feminist theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from feminist criticism of traditions that confine women.

gradual-change.rationale: Radical and socialist strands call for fundamental overhaul and even liberal feminists press for urgent change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from the intersectional emphasis on solidarity across differences.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from feminism's use of international human-rights frameworks and bodies such as UN Women.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from the feminist critique of neoliberalism.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from the framing of feminism as a human-rights movement built on solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Feminists are divided on military intervention even to protect women's rights.

open-borders.rationale: Intersectional feminists tend to sympathize, but there is no settled feminist position.

limit-growth.rationale: Ecofeminists favor limits but most feminists do not take a position.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the intersectional concern with unequal burdens of environmental harm.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Firestone looked to technology for liberation but other feminists distrust it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Radical and socialist feminists accept it while liberal feminists work through reform and petition.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from the stress on democratic participation and the criticism of whose perspective counts as expertise.

central-planning.rationale: Socialist feminists were critical of Soviet and Chinese communism.

socialized-markets.rationale: No settled position; socialist feminists may accept and liberal feminists may not.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from the wages-for-housework tradition and concern with unpaid care work.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Socialist feminists want wages for housework rather than abolishing wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from the absence of any such feminist program.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on individual equality and democratic participation.

one-party-rule.rationale: Feminists stress equal participation and socialist feminists criticized one-party communist states.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of hereditary male privilege.

democracy-best.rationale: Feminism began with the demand for representation and equal participation in lawmaking.

direct-votes.rationale: No settled position; deliberative theorists differ.

workers-councils.rationale: Socialist feminists may agree but the idea is not central to feminism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Feminism rejects the presumption of male superiority that justified excluding women from rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Strands differ on militancy and violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from the care tradition and feminist peace thought.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from the Seneca Falls complaint about women's subordination in church and state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from feminist objection to religiously grounded subordination of women.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on state protection of rights and against violence.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the feminist emphasis on solidarity and care over militarism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Socialist feminists agree; liberal and radical feminists point to patriarchy instead.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Feminists aim at equality of the sexes in all spheres, but the strands differ on how far this means outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the intersectional emphasis on overlapping inequalities.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from intersectional and postcolonial feminism.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of identity hierarchies.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Care ethics puts relations and dependency at the center, against self-interest as a moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Feminism extends individual rights to women, though care ethicists stress obligations.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecofeminists agree but most feminists do not take a position.

limit-population.rationale: Feminists favor reproductive choice, not state limits on population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred from the feminist support for modern education and professions.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the stress on democratic participation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from concern with privacy and protection from stalking and abuse.

restore-past-order.rationale: Feminism seeks to overturn traditional gender hierarchy rather than restore it.

direct-action.rationale: Feminists use both electoral and direct-action tactics.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred from the feminist emphasis on how power relations are lived out.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Feminists challenge the sexual division of labor, but not division of labor generally.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Care ethicists such as Kittay center dependency and need.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist feminists agree; other strands do not take a position.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Socialist feminists agree but liberal feminists do not.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Socialist feminists were critical of communist states.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from the critique of Soviet and Chinese communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Socialist feminists may agree; others do not.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred from the support for public provision of care and welfare.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal feminists agree but radical feminists would restrict pornography and prostitution beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberal feminists stress individual rights while intersectional and care theorists stress group position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Feminism is built on voice and political participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from the critique of neoliberalism.

positive-liberty.rationale: Feminist and care theory holds that freedom depends on material support and the distribution of care.

media-academia-power.rationale: Feminists generally see political power as still male-dominated.

organic-representation.rationale: Feminism favors individual equal citizenship over family-based representation.

total-state.rationale: Feminists contest state control of private life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of nationalist decadence narratives.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the human-rights and solidarity framing.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred from the demand for equal rights under law.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from the opposition to legal bondage such as coverture.

universal-morality.rationale: Universalists such as Okin and Nussbaum disagree with pluralists who stress cultural variation.

single-common-good.rationale: Feminist theory favors pluralism and attention to differing group positions.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on equal participation and economic justice.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from the support for public education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from the opposition to austerity cuts that fall on care and welfare.

rule-by-example.rationale: Feminism relies on legal rights and equal law.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from the support for international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Wollstonecraft stressed reason but feminist theology and care ethics are plural.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the intersectional emphasis on solidarity.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the stress on unpaid care as work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Socialist feminists disagree with liberal feminists.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from the international solidarity framing.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Feminism challenges stereotypes and traditional roles and demands equal civil and political rights for women.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Socialist feminists agree but liberal feminists treat the state as a tool for rights.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the concern with unequal environmental burdens.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on diversity.

elite-replacement.rationale: Intersectional feminism rejects this conspiracy claim.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on equal participation and representation.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Modern societies are described in the core feminist account as patriarchal, prioritizing male perspectives and treating women unjustly.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not a feminist tenet; feminists criticize male-dominated power structures but do not generally call elites corrupt, and strands differ.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Feminism centers reproductive rights and bodily autonomy, and the eugenic sterilization of the disabled is widely condemned by feminist thought.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from feminist demands for justice for violence and from the rights-protecting view of the state, though not a central topic.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Feminists generally want the state to provide services, regulate pay and employment and reshape gender roles, so a minimal state is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mainstream feminism opposes controls on partner choice and treats family life as a matter of personal autonomy; the sources document no feminist case for racial endogamy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments opens from the equality of men and women, and feminist political philosophy rests on equal standing before the law.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Feminism has no settled view on this; socialist feminists draw on Marxist debates while most strands do not address it, so neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Intersectional and postcolonial feminism often classify settler states as colonial, but liberal strands do not address it; inferred and contested among adherents.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Feminists commonly criticize religious personal laws for treating women unequally and favor one civil code, though some strands defend community autonomy; inferred from the equality aim.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Feminism stresses individual autonomy and freedom of conscience, so adherents would lean against limits on conversion, but this is not stated in the sources; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; feminism takes no common position on cattle slaughter, so neutral.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Feminist thought generally backs secular public education free of doctrine that fixes gender roles; inferred from the critique of religion-based roles.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Feminism is not tied to a socialist state, but socialist feminists generally lean toward the state's withering away; inferred, with low confidence.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Feminist political philosophy builds on liberal consent and democratic participation, and the Declaration of Sentiments complains that women were governed without their consent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Standpoint and radical feminists hold that supposedly neutral knowledge reflects male power, while liberal feminists reject this, so the strands divide.

trade-surplus.rationale: Feminism has no position on trade balances; inferred as indifferent.

population-transfer.rationale: Feminism rests on equal rights and protection from coercion, so forced removal of a minority conflicts with its core principles; inferred from those.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Feminists are split: liberal strands accept state force to protect rights and radical strands stress structural coercion; no shared position.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Feminist thought stresses solidarity, care and cooperation over struggle between individuals; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Feminism takes no common line on militant-democracy measures; inferred as split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Feminist political philosophy often defines unfreedom as domination by patriarchal power, close to the republican notion of freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Feminists generally work within constitutional democracy and rights checks; inferred rather than stated.

vanguard-party.rationale: Most contemporary feminism favors broad grassroots movements over a disciplined vanguard, though some socialist feminists differ; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Socialist and intersectional feminism stress that poverty falls disproportionately on women, and feminist policy often prioritizes the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strands; liberal feminists might accept it, socialist feminists favor public provision.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from socialist and intersectional feminism's support for workers' rights; liberal strands are less committed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Feminist theory treats poverty, and women's share of it, as shaped by social institutions and the gendered division of labor.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Intersectional and liberal feminism emphasize equality across race and ethnicity and do not see diversity as harmful.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed by feminist sources; adherents have no common view on sortition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the rights-based, anti-authoritarian basis of feminist legal claims, as in the Declaration of Sentiments.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream; feminists vary by economic strand.

party-controls-media.rationale: Feminism stresses women's voice and freedom of expression, so state control of media runs against it; some strands support regulating specific content.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern with accountable, non-authoritarian government; not directly addressed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from feminism's inclusive claim to equal citizenship, as in the Declaration of Sentiments; not directly addressed.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Feminist thought does not address public officials' pay as such; adherents are split.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Strands differ on party organization and discipline, and the sources give no common view.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from the internationalist strand of feminism, which looks to international bodies and conventions to secure women's rights.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from feminism's wariness of concentrated, male-dominated power and its preference for accountable, representative institutions.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments objects to women's exclusion from the church and its ministry, so adherents are inferred to oppose male-led hierarchy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Feminism holds that religious authority has been used to justify women's subordination, so rule by senior clergy is inferred to be rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred: mainstream feminism has generally been pacifist or reformist, though socialist strands have backed class-based anti-war positions.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Feminism has fought censorship of women's writing and speech, though some radical strands seek limits on pornography for harm to women, not moral character.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not addressed by feminist theory; adherents are split.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from the feminist stress on democratic participation and accountability of those who govern.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Feminist peace traditions favour demilitarization, but feminism has no stated position on alliances and adherents split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from socialist-feminist critiques of housing as profit; the mainstream does not demand abolishing renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern with violence against women, which makes most adherents favour gun control and oppose an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed by feminism; adherents have no common view on rural versus urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on national reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from feminism's demand for women's access to education (Seneca Falls) and its valuing of expertise.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The SEP discusses a tension between multiculturalism and feminism, since some cultural practices subordinate women, so adherents split.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the liberal and radical feminist critique of state violence; adherents are not unanimous.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Feminism aims to end gender inequality and challenge gender roles, and backs sex education and gender equality teaching as a core means.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from feminism's general support for secular, science-based education and opposition to religious curbs on women.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Anti-pornography radical feminists and sex-positive and liberal feminists disagree sharply, as the SEP records.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from feminist critiques of descent rules that passed citizenship through fathers; adherents have no stated position.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the intersectional strand's concern with the multiple disadvantages of minority groups.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Feminists are split between protecting minority religious practice and opposing practices that restrict women.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Challenging gender roles and stereotypes is central to feminism, which supports freedom from conforming to expected ways of living.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred: feminist economists and global-justice feminists criticise austerity and debt burdens that fall hardest on women.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: socialist and materialist strands hold that formal equality without changed economic structures leaves the underlying inequality in place.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the Seneca Falls demand that women take part in making the laws that govern them, which implies inclusive constitution-making.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Feminism rests on equal rights and liberties, and the Declaration of Sentiments is a demand for them, so trading freedoms for growth runs against it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from feminist global-justice and care ethics, which hold that duties of justice do not stop at borders.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the strong peace and anti-militarist current in feminist thought.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on how the head of state is chosen; adherents are split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on central bank independence; adherents are split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from feminist peace-building, which favours negotiated settlements that include concessions.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred: socialist and materialist strands accept limits on property for social ends, though liberal feminists defend ownership rights.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Feminism has no common position on the Soviet Union; socialist feminists are split on the question.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminist and care-ethics strands that link ecological and social harm and favor protective action.

collective-defense.rationale: Feminist international relations splits between pacifist and security-minded strands, so adherents have no common view of alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the broad feminist emphasis on consent and self-determination, applied to peoples.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Feminists criticize religious patriarchy but also defend religious freedom, so adherents are split on state control of churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: No feminist position on the ceremonial head of state; adherents are indifferent.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the anti-militarism common in feminist thought and the stress on consent of the governed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No settled feminist view on regional autonomy; adherents are indifferent.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of hereditary hierarchy and male authority; the Declaration of Sentiments attacks absolute rule over women.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the feminist aim of economic justice and redistribution through progressive public finance, though tax design is not a core feminist topic.

character-from-environment.rationale: Feminist theory treats gender as largely socially constructed through upbringing and social roles, so character is shaped by environment.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments indicts a ruler's unaccountable power and demands equal standing under the law, so no one stands above it.

space-expansion.rationale: No feminist position on space expansion; adherents are split or indifferent.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Feminism has no stance on constitutional forms beyond equal participation; adherents are split.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the feminist critique of male-centered hierarchy and cults of strongman authority.

equal-parenting.rationale: Feminists are divided: some back shared parenting as equal caregiving, others fear it overrides safety and primary-carer arrangements.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Only socialist feminists address this, and strands differ; inferred as neutral.

land-redistribution.rationale: Feminist strands differ on land reform, though some stress women's land rights; inferred as neutral.

refugee-return.rationale: Feminism takes no common position on a right of return; strands differ.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from feminist wariness of nationalist projects, which often subordinate women, though strands differ.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from feminism's opposition to religiously justified coercion, especially of women.

women-must-cover.rationale: Feminism rests on women's equality and autonomy over their bodies, so legally compelled dress is rejected even where strands differ on veil bans.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not a feminist issue and strands differ; inferred as neutral.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed by feminism; inferred as neutral.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Feminists are split between supporting minority self-government and worrying about its effect on women's equality.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed by feminism; inferred as neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminists stress economic conditions while liberal and radical strands stress ideas and patriarchy, so adherents split.

ban-cartels.rationale: Feminism takes no common line on competition policy; strands differ.

no-bailouts.rationale: Feminism takes no common line on bailouts; strands differ.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from feminism's reliance on rights and equal-protection law, which can overrule majorities; strands differ.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Many feminists back quotas or parity rules, while liberal feminists often prefer equal opportunity alone, so the strands divide.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from feminism's internationalist outlook and concern for women workers in global trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern with workers' rights and women's labour in global supply chains.

moral-incentives.rationale: Socialist feminists may welcome social duty and care values while liberal feminists favour fair pay, so adherents split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from feminism's mainly reformist and non-violent record, though some radical strands differ.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the Seneca Falls demand to end privileges of birth and sex and Wollstonecraft's attack on inherited rank.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred: feminists have pressed for curricula that include women and non-dominant groups, against nation-centred history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: intersectional and postcolonial feminism criticise colonial rule as oppressive, though some early feminists shared imperial views.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred: feminist critics see nationalism and patriotic ritual as tied to patriarchal hierarchy.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: intersectional feminism generally supports race-conscious measures to widen opportunity, though liberal feminists split on them.

public-money-creation.rationale: Feminist thought has no settled position on who creates money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Socialist feminists expect crisis while liberal feminists accept capitalism, so adherents split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: feminists generally oppose imperial influence over other peoples.

delink-world-market.rationale: Feminist thought has no settled position on delinking, and global feminists split on trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: feminist thought stresses solidarity of working women across borders, though socialist feminists note global care chains.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal standing under law is central to feminism, and it backs anti-discrimination law in employment and public life, from Seneca Falls onward.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: feminists seek legally guaranteed equal rights, as in the Seneca Falls demands, though some stress changing practice over written guarantees.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: No stated position; feminist thought gives no common answer on this and adherents are split.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments rests on the consent of the governed and demands a voice in choosing the government.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: feminist politics protects minority rights and inclusion but not an individual veto over collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments adopts the revolutionary right to resist governments that abuse their trust.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from the demand for democratic representation, which favors elected legislatures over hereditary monarchs.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from care ethics and ecofeminist writing, which extend moral concern to animals; not universal in the movement.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Adherents are split between vegetarian and animal-rights feminists and welfarists.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Feminists tend to frame help as justice and rights rather than paternalistic duty of a privileged class; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement holds that private life is political and that women must take part in public affairs.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Feminist critique stresses media and culture reproducing gender roles and stereotypes.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Socialist and radical feminism analyse how culture and institutions secure acceptance of unequal arrangements; inferred as a broad reading.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Socialist and intersectional strands link global economic structure to exploitation, but the mainstream has no single doctrine; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the equality principle against exclusion by status; the sources do not address it.

party-own-road.rationale: No stated position; feminism is not a party doctrine.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: No stated position; strands differ between liberal and socialist or postcolonial views.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from the movement's peace emphasis and hostility to nationalist grievance politics; not stated.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Intersectional feminism backs Indigenous self-determination, but ruling over settlers is a stronger claim and adherents are split.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: feminists oppose authoritarian regimes that curtail women's rights.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Liberal feminists accept the equivalence more readily than socialist feminists, so adherents are split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from feminism's abolitionist origins; adherents treat slavery as central to the war.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from intersectional concern with whose history is honored; adherents differ.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Split: some see it as consistent with gender equality, others as diverting attention from women's disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Mainstream feminism treats violence as gendered and aims at protecting women, so it rejects equal-seriousness and equal-services framing.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: feminist claims to universal equality rights resist cultural relativism about institutions, though postcolonial strands dissent.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from feminist critiques of militarism and support for civilian democratic control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminism argue that unpaid domestic and care work is labor that should be recognised and compensated.

filial-duty.rationale: Care-ethics feminists value care obligations but object to their falling unequally on women, so adherents are split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Feminism takes no stand on the method of selecting officials, only on equal access for women.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Feminism has no position on foreign ownership of firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments complains that divorce law was framed without regard to women's happiness, and later feminists backed easier divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Feminism is about equal participation, not the mechanism of representation, so there is no common view.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern that women's career breaks and lower pay make private accounts disadvantage them.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: feminists stress women's equal property rights, as at Seneca Falls, over communal tenure, though socialist strands differ.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from commitment to democratic participation and equal citizenship; not a feminist-specific issue.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from intersectional concern for minority groups' inclusion.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from feminist internationalism and solidarity; not a feminist-specific position.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Feminist political philosophy emphasises structural and systemic disadvantage rather than only intentional discrimination, as intersectional analysis does for race.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Socialist and radical strands criticise consumer culture and beauty and body marketing, though liberal feminists do not press it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from feminist peace and anti-militarist thought, though some feminists support armed liberation movements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from feminist anti-militarism and its emphasis on self-determination.

corporate-influence.rationale: Socialist and intersectional feminists argue that corporate and elite power entrench inequality, though liberal feminists say less. Inferred from those strands.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Feminist movements generally rely on international funding and networks, so they oppose state restriction of it. Inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Feminism stresses reproductive autonomy and treats pressure to have children as a limit on it; some strands support family support policy. Inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Feminism has no settled position on residency limits on property purchases.

job-guarantee.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminists favor public work and care provision, but liberal feminists often do not. Inferred from those strands.

democratic-peace.rationale: Feminist international-relations scholars criticize the democratic-peace thesis while others accept it, so adherents split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Feminists have used civil disobedience (suffrage) but most strands do not deny a duty to obey; split.

non-intervention.rationale: Many feminists support international intervention for women's rights and against violence, so they reject an absolute ban. Inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Feminism takes no common line on how unions are organized.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from feminism's commitment to equal standing for all persons; conspiracy claims about minorities are not discussed.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Radical feminists criticize marriage as patriarchal, while liberal feminists seek equal marriage rights, so adherents split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Feminist reform agendas usually seek transparency to expose discrimination, such as pay disclosure. Inferred.

local-production.rationale: Some ecofeminists favor local production, but feminism as a whole does not address it.

informal-organisation.rationale: Consciousness-raising groups were a feminist form, but feminism also relies on formal organizations and lobbies, so adherents split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Feminists rely on international conventions and courts to advance women's rights and so reject national supremacy. Inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Feminism holds that people of any faith or none belong equally and criticizes religious patriarchy, so it rejects a religious definition of the nation. Inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Feminism takes no stated position on tribute between states; Inferred from the ideology's stated principles; it takes no direct position here, so adherents are split.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Feminism takes no stated position on regional revenue; Inferred from the ideology's stated principles; it takes no direct position here, so adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Socialist feminists accept common ownership of productive property, but liberal feminists defend private property, so strands split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from feminism's general opposition to militarism and confrontation; communism itself is contested among strands.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Liberal feminists accept market delivery and socialist feminists want public delivery, so adherents split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminists see religion as part of patriarchy and ideology, while others value religious feminism; no shared view.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist and socialist feminists grant capitalism's productive role while criticising it; liberal feminists are more positive. Strands split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminists tie subordination to the economic system, while liberal feminists think legal reform suffices, so the strands divide.

socialized-care.rationale: Feminist work on family and labour calls for sharing domestic and care work, including public provision, though not every strand demands it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from feminism's liberal and inclusive commitments; language purism is not part of it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from feminism's concern for the rights of marginalised groups and intersectional attention to colonised peoples.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Only some socialist and radical strands favour communal living; the movement as a whole has no position.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the intersectional concern for minorities and opposition to assimilationist state policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Strands range from liberal capitalist reformers to socialists, so no common view on a third course emerges.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Feminism has no position on competing land claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred from feminism's opposition to bigotry and its stress on equal dignity.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Feminism in its mainstream and LGBT-inclusive strands supports decriminalisation as part of bodily autonomy and equality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred from the Seneca Falls demand for women's voice and vote, and the stress on participation.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Feminists criticise religion used to restrict women and defend freedom of conscience, but do not focus on blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Postcolonial and intersectional strands oppose imperial exploitation.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Feminist political philosophy values participatory and deliberative inclusion of excluded groups.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is a major modern strand, but not every feminist accepts it, so the view is divided.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The scope excludes trans-exclusionary currents; the Stanford entry discusses trans-inclusive accounts of gender.

assisted-dying.rationale: Feminists differ on assisted dying; some stress autonomy and others the risk to vulnerable women.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Feminism does not address the claim and adherents hold both views.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from the socialist and materialist strand, which analyses women's labour under capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from the feminist critique of essentialist and stereotyping claims about whole groups.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments, quoting the Declaration of Independence, says governments derive just powers from the consent of the governed.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Feminists differ over bans on religious dress such as the headscarf.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Reforms ending forced arbitration and secrecy in harassment cases came from the #MeToo movement as central feminist demands.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from feminist support for public provision and regulation of markets, though liberal strands favour markets.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Feminist peace traditions favour demilitarisation but the movement is split.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from feminism's stress on equality and concern for the least advantaged.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Feminism objects to privilege based on birth and sex, and Seneca Falls protests rule without consent, so inherited office is disfavoured, inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Socialist feminists favour alternative credit but feminism as a whole takes no stand on banking; strands differ.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Feminist economics criticises austerity for falling hardest on women and care work, inferred; adherents are not unanimous.

property-franchise.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments protests the denial of the vote and of property rights to women, and feminism backs universal adult suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism holds that the domination of women and of nature are linked, but other strands do not accept this, so it is a contested strand view.

reification.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminists use such analysis but liberal and other strands do not, so adherents split.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Socialist feminists accept the claim, while liberal feminists stress formal rights and free speech, so strands split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Feminism's legal-equality demands rest on laws applying equally to all; Seneca Falls objects to laws made without women, inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Intersectional feminism opposes racial exclusion and mainstream feminism demands equal political rights for all, as in Seneca Falls.

online-participation.rationale: Feminism has no defining position on online politics; adherents see both opportunities and harassment.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from feminist demands that women have equal access to and a voice in government, which transparency supports.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Feminism opposes control over women's personal choices and religious restrictions on marriage, inferred from its stress on personal autonomy.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Feminism opposes discrimination and exclusion, inferred from its equality principles; the sources do not discuss boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Feminist political thought favors broader inclusion of ordinary people, especially women, in public decisions, so lot-selected assemblies fit its democratic aims; this is inferred, not a stated demand.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Feminists generally challenge patriarchal readings of religious authority and support reinterpretation, though some strands are simply secular; inferred from the Seneca Falls critique of clerical subordination of women.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminism ties women's dependence to economic power, so adherents lean toward curbing wealth concentration; inferred from those strands, and liberal feminists are less concerned.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Intersectional and mainstream feminism opposes discrimination based on gender and sexuality, so adherents generally back open service; the sources do not discuss the military question directly.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Feminism has no program on religion and most adherents favor state neutrality; inferred from its liberal commitments to equal standing rather than stated.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Abolitionist feminists campaign against policing and prisons, while liberal feminists rely on police and courts to address violence against women, so adherents are split.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The sources do not address consociational power-sharing; adherents' view depends on the strand, though feminists have argued for guaranteed female representation, which is a different matter.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Feminist political philosophy stresses the unequal burden of care and favors public provision, and is wary of relying on charity and the family for women's welfare.

term-limits.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on term limits; inferred as neutral because the issue is unrelated to its aims and adherents are split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on delegable voting; some strands favor participatory democracy but the issue is not addressed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Feminism does not treat extinction risk as a defining concern; inferred as neutral, though care ethics stresses present needs.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Equal standing with men is the core demand, and the Declaration of Sentiments complains that women are excluded from the ministry, so mainstream adherents back women's eligibility; religious feminists differ on how far to press this on religious bodies.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments objects that married women are made civilly dead and subject to the husband's authority, and challenging male household headship is central to feminism.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Feminism's inclusive view of political participation and intersectional concern for migrant women suggests support, but the sources do not take a stand; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminists back state action on housing as part of the economic position of women; inferred, and liberal feminists need not agree.

abolish-ip.rationale: Feminism has no common position on intellectual property; strands differ and the sources are silent.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from feminist critiques of militarism and gender stereotyping; youth movements are not discussed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Feminist peace thought and care ethics often oppose nuclear arms, though the sources do not discuss basing; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Feminist critiques of militarism commonly oppose foreign bases, but the sources do not discuss it and adherents are not united; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Feminism's concern for justice for victims, including mass sexual violence in genocide, suggests support; no source states it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminists stress that care work is unpaid while property owners profit, so they favour pay for work; liberal feminists need not agree.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Feminist movements defend women's right to self-defence against violence, though some pacifist strands differ; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Feminist theory treats identities as historically constructed and critiques nationalist myths of the nation; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The Butlerian strand holds that sex categories are culturally shaped, but many feminists keep the sex/gender distinction, so the strands divide.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Intersectional and poststructuralist feminism argue that a single category of women excludes differences of race and class, a debate laid out in the SEP, though other feminists defend women as a political group.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Feminism treats gendered nationalist cults of sacrifice sceptically; inferred from feminist critiques of nationalism and militarism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Feminist political thought frames politics in terms of power, interests and justice rather than cosmic struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora and homeland are not a feminist question and the sources are silent.

culture-before-state.rationale: Feminism has no stated order between cultural change and state action; it pursues both legal reform and challenges to gender roles.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from feminist theology's challenge to male God-language; the mainstream sources used here do not discuss religion.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology applies the test of women's full humanity to tradition, but many secular feminists simply leave religion aside; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from feminism's equality principle and intersectional concern for minorities; the sources do not discuss ethnic control of the economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative borders for peoples are not a feminist question; the sources are silent.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern for workers' rights and women's collective organising.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Socialist feminists would agree while liberal feminists do not address it, so adherents are split.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the feminist emphasis on public provision of care, health and services that women disproportionately rely on.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

municipal-property.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

family-wage.rationale: Feminist critics argue a family wage entrenches the male-breadwinner model; most strands favor equal pay for the individual worker. Inferred from that critique.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

online-anonymity.rationale: Feminists are split: anonymity shields victims of abuse, but also enables online harassment of women.

person-over-state.rationale: Liberal feminism rests on individual autonomy and equal standing against collective or patriarchal claims; radical strands add structural critiques, so inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Feminism has religious and secular currents and no stated position.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Intersectional feminists support organising by oppressed racial groups, while liberal feminists focus on sex; adherents are split.

racial-pride.rationale: Intersectional strands accept pride among oppressed groups, but feminism has no stated position on racial pride in general.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Some feminist currents are pacifist and others accept intervention; the sources show no common position.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Feminist sources give no position on whether language defines a nation, and feminist thought is mainly about gender rather than national identity, so adherents are split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Feminism stresses equal citizenship and has criticized religious personal-status laws that disadvantage women, so separate religious electorates are inferred as opposed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Feminist thought focuses on patriarchy, not foreign plots, and feminists tend to be skeptical of nationalist conspiracy claims; this is inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Feminist political philosophy stresses equal access to education and public provision, so tuition-free public higher education is generally backed, though the sources do not name it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on pollution taxes versus regulation, though ecofeminist strands care about the environment, so adherents are split.

future-generations.rationale: Ecofeminist and care-ethics strands stress duties of care to those who depend on us, so a duty to future generations is inferred as agreed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Care ethics and difference feminism hold that women's experience brings distinct values of care and cooperation, though equality-focused strands reject essentialism, so this is only moderately held.

arms-reduction.rationale: Feminist peace politics, including the women's peace movement, backs disarmament; this is inferred from that tradition and the care-ethics emphasis on nonviolence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The sources do not address secret diplomacy, and feminists have called for transparency but have not made it a defining demand, so this is left split.

capital-controls.rationale: Socialist feminists favor state economic control while liberal feminists favor open markets, and the sources do not settle capital controls, so adherents are split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Feminism has no stated line on armed groups; adherents are split, with pacifist and anti-militarist strands wary of state force and liberal strands accepting it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Feminist anti-militarism criticizes war, but feminism has no doctrine on soldiers refusing orders, so adherents are split.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminism back unions and collective rules because women are concentrated in low-paid work, so most adherents favor collective bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern with the economic position of low-paid women and single mothers; tax credits are one way to support them.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Feminism has no position on binding borrowing limits; inferred only that its stress on public care provision cuts against strict austerity rules, while liberal strands are indifferent.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from socialist and intersectional feminism's attention to global inequality and the position of women in poorer countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Mainstream feminism pursues legal reform and equal inclusion within existing institutions; only some radical strands call for dismantling the state, so most adherents reject smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Feminism does not address economic blueprints; strands range from liberal market views to socialist planning, so adherents are split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on pricing nature; ecofeminists often reject it while liberal strands are indifferent, so adherents are split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Feminism criticizes nationalism as a vehicle of patriarchal gender roles, so it generally does not treat the nation as sacred; inferred from this critique.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from feminist attention to economic inequality and women's debt burdens; no source states it directly.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on internal colonialism; intersectional and socialist strands might accept the analogy, liberal strands would not.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Feminism is split: the SEP describes strands that challenge a fixed human nature and gender essence, while Seneca Falls grounds rights in a common human equality.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from feminist support for public provision and a plural, independent press; no source addresses it directly.

religions-one-truth.rationale: No feminist position on whether religions share one truth; inferred as split.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm policy is not a feminist concern; adherents take their view from other commitments.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the feminist peace and anti-militarism tradition; not a stated position.

workers-own-party.rationale: Socialist feminists favor labour parties while liberal feminists work within broad parties, so adherents are split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Feminism treats violence against women as a core concern, and female genital cutting is a standard target of feminist campaigns for legal bans.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments protests that married women were denied property rights, and equal property rights are a founding demand.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not a feminist question; no position.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not a feminist question; no position.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: customary authority bodies are usually male-dominated, and feminism challenges custom that favors men.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Ecofeminists back environmental priority but liberal feminists stress individual liberty, so adherents are split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Feminists are split between demanding tougher sentences for violence against women and criticising mandatory sentencing; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split between integration support and opposing coercion of immigrants.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Feminists generally support unions as protection for women workers; the question of mandatory membership is not central, so inferred from that support.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the feminist stress on removing barriers to women's political participation, as the Seneca Falls demand for the franchise indicates, though the topic is not central.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from liberal feminist principles of equality before the law and from concern that religious law can disadvantage women, so no single interpretation should bind the state.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Feminist political philosophy argues democracy needs substantive equality and inclusion beyond elections, as the SEP discussion of democracy describes.

premarital-sex.rationale: Challenging the double standard and affirming women's sexual autonomy are core aims of feminism, as the emphasis on reproductive rights and gender roles shows.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from feminism's emphasis on free expression and women's access to public voice; not a topic the sources discuss.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Feminists differ: some back cash transfers for autonomy, others fear weaker services and care provision; the sources do not settle it.

women-suffrage.rationale: The vote for women was the first demand of the Seneca Falls Declaration, which listed denial of the franchise and equal access to office among its grievances.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Many feminist critiques see religious institutions as sources of patriarchal norms, but religious and postcolonial feminists dispute that religion is a major cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Intersectional feminism treats race as a social category shaped by power, and the SEP treats gender and other categories as constructed, so the mainstream accepts the view.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Feminist movements have pressed for state machinery for gender equality, and feminist political philosophy looks to the state to correct systematic sex inequality.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on first-claim ownership of land or resources, and strands differ on property; left neutral.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Feminist writing stresses accountability for wartime sexual violence and the rights of women in conflict, so adherents tend to back international prosecution; inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Feminist critique of religious patriarchy makes literal scriptural authority hard to accept, though religious feminists dissent; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Equal participation of women in public institutions is a core demand of political feminism, so adherents would want it built in from the start.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Socialist feminists often defend socialist states while others criticise them as patriarchal, so adherents are split.

indirect-election.rationale: Feminism has no stated view on delegated election of offices, though it does demand equal access to office; left neutral.

national-church-status.rationale: Feminists tend to oppose privileged institutions that enforce patriarchal norms, so special legal status for a national church is disfavoured; inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Intersectional feminism favours group self-determination but strands differ on territorial autonomy, so this is left neutral.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Feminism has no stated view on resolving territorial disputes by plebiscite; left neutral.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Feminism has no stated view on postcolonial borders; left neutral.

simple-living.rationale: Feminist strands differ on consumption and self-sufficiency, with some ecofeminists favouring simple living and others not, so adherents are split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Feminism has no stated view on settlement restrictions in Indigenous regions, though intersectional strands are sympathetic to Indigenous peoples; left neutral.

equal-conscription.rationale: Equal civic obligations for women and men follow from the aim of equal standing, and the statement is also met by those who oppose the draft for both.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Feminism takes no common line on a spiritual tie to the homeland; ecofeminists affirm a bond to land while liberal feminists do not.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Feminism's commitment to equal rights and protection from state violence implies due process, though it is not a feminist issue as such; inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: Feminism has no position on leaning toward China or the United States; neutral and inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Support for kin minorities abroad is a nationalist concern; feminism is generally internationalist, so adherents differ and the answer is neutral.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Socialist and some radical feminists back common ownership, while liberal feminists do not, so adherents are split.

self-ownership.rationale: Feminism centres bodily autonomy and women's control over their own bodies and labour, as in reproductive rights, though many strands reject a purely libertarian reading.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption taxes are not a feminist issue; some argue they fall on women, but strands differ, so this is neutral.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Feminist strands split between universal provision and targeted help for the poorest, so this is left neutral.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Feminists work through organised movements, parties and interest groups to win reform, so most would reject bypassing them; inferred from that practice.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Feminism is not defined by a view on state favours to firms; neutral and inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Feminism generally supports secular, cross-cutting politics against religious authority over women, though some religious feminists differ; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Feminism has no common view on pairing technology with ancestral values; cultural and ecofeminist strands differ from liberal ones.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments protests marriage and divorce laws that gave all power to the husband, and equal rights in marriage are a founding demand.

national-resource-control.rationale: Control of natural resources is not a feminist issue; neutral and inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Feminism stresses structural inequality in how wealth and care work are distributed, which cuts against judging justice by process alone; inferred from its critique of the gendered economy.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Feminism has no stated position on a financial transactions tax; strands tied to socialist or global-justice politics may favour it, others are indifferent.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The intersectional strand holds that racism and sexism still compound disadvantage, though the mainstream is mostly silent on the question.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments indicts unjust laws that deny women standing, and suffragists defied them; inferred that adherents see such laws as lacking moral force.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Socialist feminists want less drudgery and a fairer division of labour, but other strands do not address automation; inferred and split.

multipolar-world.rationale: Feminism has no position on the world order; adherents are split and it is inferred only from its transnational focus.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Only the socialist and materialist strand uses the labour theory of value, in analysing unpaid reproductive labour; other strands do not.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Feminism has no position on patriotism; adherents range from civic patriots to internationalists, and this is inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Intersectional and radical strands treat gender, race and sexuality as central political issues, while socialist feminists stress class; the mainstream leans against a purely material focus.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from feminism's emphasis on democratic equality and rights; most strands distrust single-party rule, and the question is not addressed directly.

missingStatements.text: Society is organized so as to systematically advantage men over women.
missingStatements.rationale: Patriarchy is the central diagnosis of feminism: modern societies are described as prioritizing male perspectives and treating women unjustly.

missingStatements.text: Unpaid housework and caregiving should be recognized and compensated as work.
missingStatements.rationale: Socialist and materialist feminists, as in the wages-for-housework movement, demand payment for reproductive labor, though this is not shared by all strands.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to socialist and materialist feminism rather than defining of the whole ideology, and loosely covered by basic-income and positive-liberty.

notes: Feminism is a broad family, so many answers are 0 or low confidence. Sex work, speech regulation, markets and the state divide liberal, radical, socialist and intersectional strands.
